subject: Pilot structure: timebox vs credit-based evaluation for Atlas Retail
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara@atlasretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question on pilot structure for Atlas Retail

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — our ML and product teams liked the throughput numbers. We are trying to decide internally between two pilot styles and I wanted to get your guidance:

1) Timeboxed pilot: 45 days of evaluation with access to the Hosted API, usage capped at ~100k tokens/day.
2) Credit-based pilot: $8k platform credit applied to usage until exhausted, typically used over 60 days.

Procurement flagged that credits complicate PO and invoicing; they prefer a simple time extension. From a product POV, our team likes the credit model because it mirrors anticipated spend.

Can Redwood do a hybrid? e.g., a 45-day guaranteed window plus a small credit pool for burst testing? Also curious if a short term discount (e.g., 20% off first month of committed capacity) is something you can approve.

Appreciate a quick note on what others do and what you'd recommend given our use case (real-time product experiments + nightly batch embedding jobs).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Klein
VP of ML, Atlas Retail

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara@atlasretail.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on pilot structure for Atlas Retail

Hi Sara — great to hear the demo landed well. Short answer: yes, we offer both patterns and hybrids; the right choice depends on procurement and your evaluation goals. Options we typically recommend: 

Option A — Timebox-focused (team-favorite for procurement):
- 45-day hosted evaluation window
- Usage cap: 100k tokens/day (burst allowance up to 150k/day for 2 non-consecutive days)
- Includes prefix caching and one performance tuning session with our infra team
- No invoicing complexity beyond a single evaluation SOW

Option B — Credit-based (team-favorite for product teams):
- $8,000 platform credits assigned to your account; credits consume per-token billing as normal
- 60-day window to use credits
- Ideal for realistic usage patterns (embedding + chat)

Option C — Hybrid (what you described):
- 45-day guaranteed window + $2,500 credits for burst/edge-case testing
- Separate SOW but we can keep billing simple (single PO that references credits as pre-paid usage)

On discounts: we can offer a one-time pilot discount (we typically authorize up to 15% for POC pilots via the Growth team). For anything above that I need a quick internal approval from Marcus.

I attached a short SOW and a pricing spreadsheet with the three options. If procurement prefers a timeboxed SOW, Option A is the path of least resistance; Option C is a good compromise if you want realistic usage.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to finalize — are you available tomorrow 11/21 at 10am PT?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks, that is helpful. Procurement weighs heavily on our side; they dislike pre-paid credit constructs because they create accounting reconciliation work.

If Redwood can give us:
- Option A (45 days) + a 30% pilot-credit-equivalent discount on any overage during the pilot window (billed after the pilot as a single invoice), that would make procurement comfortable while letting our team test realistic spikes.

We also want the pilot to include an explicit conversion conversation at day 30 to surface any blockers.

Can you confirm if Redwood can commit to the "conversion conversation" and the 30% overage discount?

Thanks,
Tom

Final pilot proposal (single SOW attached):
- 45-day Hosted API evaluation window, start date to be confirmed on signature
- Baseline usage cap: 100k tokens/day, burst allowance documented (up to 150k/day for two non-consecutive days)
- Any consumption beyond the baseline cap will be billed at our standard hosted rates; Redwood will apply a 30% credit to that overage invoice as a one-time pilot concession (applied post-pilot).

- No pre-paid credits on the PO (per procurement preference)
- Pilot discount: 12% one-time credit applied to the invoice for baseline usage if they sign the SOW within 5 business days (to encourage timely start)
